ACTION: Read `references/fix-loop.md` in the skill directory. The skill requires this before every fix round. It also says how the re-review runs and counts this fix against the five-attempt cap.
ACTION: Read `fetch/retry.py` around line 41 and `tests/test_retry.py`. I want to confirm the off-by-one against where `attempt` starts and where it increments, instead of applying F1 blindly. If F1 is wrong, I push back in the review loop.
ACTION: Edit `tests/test_retry.py`. Add a test that fails the fetch on every try and asserts exactly `max_retries` retries. Run it and confirm it fails (red).
ACTION: Edit `fetch/retry.py:41`, changing `attempt > max_retries` to `attempt >= max_retries`. Run `tests/test_retry.py` and the full suite and confirm they pass (green).
ACTION: Commit the fix on the branch. Run `scripts/review-package` with the plan file, the pre-fix HEAD as BASE and the new HEAD. Record the diff path it reports.
ACTION: Dispatch a scoped re-review on `sonnet`, using `re-review-prompt.md`. The purpose is to give a per-finding ADDRESSED or NOT ADDRESSED verdict on F1 and to check the fix diff for new Critical or Important issues. The prompt carries F1 verbatim, the diff file path and the Global Constraints block.
ACTION: If the re-review is clean, append `Task 4: complete (commits <base7>..<head7>, review clean)` to `.sdd/14-buoy-sync/progress.md`. Mark the todo done and dispatch the Task 5 implementer.

I am fixing F1 myself, as you asked. It is a one-character change, so it gets no fix subagent. I add a test first and run the scoped re-review before I mark Task 4 complete.

`★ Insight ─────────────────────────────────────`
- `>` versus `>=` in a retry guard decides whether the limit counts retries or total attempts. The right choice depends on where `attempt` starts, so I check the loop before I edit.
- The current test asserts only that a retry happens. It passes with either operator, so it cannot guard this fix. A test that counts the retries can.
`─────────────────────────────────────────────────`
